builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FORALL-LEAN-AGENT for Auditable Reasoning in Formal Mathematics and Software Verification
summary: The method replaces trusting Lean compilation success alone with an auditable harness that binds statement comparison, axiom audits, fresh review, and independent proof checking to each candidate artifact. It costs additional orchestration complexity and reviewer/verifier compute per candidate, though the paper reports a small net cost reduction ($69 to $62) on VeriSoftBench. It can fail if the statement comparison or axiom audit misses semantically equivalent but weakened formulations, if the isolated workspaces or Lean toolchain versions drift, or if fresh review inherits the same blind spots as the generator model.
rationale: The reader uses third-party APIs and would benefit from auditable acceptance of agent-generated proofs or verified code, but the gains are demonstrated only on formal-math and software-verification benchmarks, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Auditable verification harness for Lean proof agents

claims.statement: The method replaces trusting Lean compilation success alone with an auditable harness that binds statement comparison, axiom audits, fresh review, and independent proof checking to each candidate artifact. It costs additional orchestration complexity and reviewer/verifier compute per candidate, though the paper reports a small net cost reduction ($69 to $62) on VeriSoftBench. It can fail if the statement comparison or axiom audit misses semantically equivalent but weakened formulations, if the isolated workspaces or Lean toolchain versions drift, or if fresh review inherits the same blind spots as the generator model.

On the 100-task VeriSoftBench subset, the framework raises benchmark-rule success from 93 to 100 for GPT-5.6 Sol at low effort while reducing cost from $69 to $62 (~1.11x cost reduction); PutnamBench accepts all 672 problems at $4.72 average per problem.
